title: Agent identity: whose permissions does an agent use?
summary: The page passes: its identity patterns, controls, runtime warnings and licensing statements are supported by Microsoft documentation. A minor correction should acknowledge that Microsoft's agent-management pages give a less demanding Conditional Access licensing requirement than its dedicated licensing section.

claims.claim: The maker-credential control is under Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: select **Manage**. ... Select **Environments** or **Environment groups**. ... select **Settings** on the top menu bar. Expand the **Product** section, and select **Features**. ... **Copilot Studio agents** ... **Control maker credential options**

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for Control maker credential options was found as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" API Power Platform PowerShell pac admin; maker credentials Power Platform API; maker credentials Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and returned PowerShell/CLI excerpts; none documented this operation.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials sharing setting is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Go to **Manage** > **Environments**, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select **Settings**, and then select **Features**. ... Find **Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials**.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the embedded-maker-credentials sharing control was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" API PowerShell Power Platform. Read configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials, the Security control page, and returned settings-features and PowerShell excerpts; no equivalent call was documented.

claims.claim: A connector tool's credential choice is under Agents > agent > Tools > tool > Overview > Details > Additional details > Credentials to use in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** and select the agent ... Go to the **Tools** page ... Go to the connector tool **Overview** page. ... Under **Details** > **Additional details** > **Credentials to use**, select **Maker-provided credentials**.

claims.claim: No documented automation equivalent was found for selecting each connector tool's credentials.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio connector tool "Credentials to use" Dataverse Web API authentication; botcomponent connection authentication maker credentials API. Read advanced-connectors and returned configure-enduser-authentication and CLI excerpts; consent bypass is a different setting.

claims.claim: Dataverse agent users are added under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Agents > + Add agent in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: select **Manage**. ... select **Environments**. ... choose an environment. ... select **Settings**. ... Expand **Users + permissions**, and then select **Agents**. ... Select **+ Add agent** from the command bar.

claims.claim: No API for adding an Entra-linked Dataverse agent user was found as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users API add agent systemuser; agent users Dataverse Web API create; agent user Add-AdminPowerAppsSyncUser. Read create-users, agent-users and returned Graph/PowerShell references; none documented adding this agent-user type to Dataverse.

claims.claim: Agent identities are viewed and managed under Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities in Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Browse to **Entra ID** > **Agents** > **Agent identities**.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity updates an agent identity.
claims.quote: Update the properties of an agentIdentity object. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity

claims.claim: Conditional Access targets agent users through Assignments > Users, agents, or workload identities > Agents.
claims.quote: under **Assignments** > **Users, agents, or workload identities**, select **Agents**, and then target all agent users or specific agent users.

claims.claim: The documented Conditional Access creation example uses POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies with a policy JSON body and configures a block policy for all agent identities in report-only state.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies ... "includeAgentIdServicePrincipals": [ "All" ] ... "builtInControls": [ "block" ] ... "state": "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"

claims.claim: Agent sign-ins are viewed under Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs in Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**.

claims.claim: The documented agent-identity sign-in query is GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'

claims.claim: With end-user credentials, the user signs into the connected service.
claims.quote: the agent prompts that user to sign in if they haven't already.

claims.claim: The end-user-authenticated action runs under that user's identity.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity.

claims.claim: An end-user-authenticated agent cannot perform an action the user lacks permission to perform.
claims.quote: If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: Maker-provided authentication uses the maker's credentials rather than the end user's.
claims.quote: the agent uses the maker's credentials, not the end user's credentials, to authenticate with connected services.

claims.claim: Maker-provided credentials can expose data or actions unavailable to the end user.
claims.quote: an end user might retrieve information or perform actions that only the maker's account is permitted to do.

claims.claim: Microsoft names service principals, API keys and managed identities as examples of approved system identities.
claims.quote: Agents that use an approved system identity, such as a service principal, API key, or managed identity, can be published when the associated connection supports the scenario.

claims.claim: A service identity's data access is governed by its granted permissions.
claims.quote: When you create service accounts for automated use, they're granted permissions to access resources in Azure and Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent can have its own identity in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: An agent identity is a special service principal in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Permissions and policies applied to an agent identity determine its access.
claims.quote: Apply a conditional access policy to all Sales Assistant Agents. ... Revoke a permission grant for all Sales Assistant agents.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs capture agent activity.
claims.quote: This article describes how agent identity activities are logged in Microsoft Entra ID and how to access those logs using the Microsoft Entra admin center and Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: What it is: after patterns table
claims.claim: The credential choice is configured on the individual connector tool.
claims.quote: Go to the connector tool **Overview** page. ... Under **Details** > **Additional details** > **Credentials to use**, select **Maker-provided credentials**.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent identity is a special service principal.
claims.quote: An agent identity is a special service principal in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity

claims.quote: Agent identities don't have credentials of their own.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: The blueprint acquires tokens on behalf of an agent identity.
claims.quote: They rely on the agent identity blueprint to acquire tokens on their behalf.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Copilot Studio automatically provisions Entra Agent IDs for new agents.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically provisions Entra Agent IDs for new agents. The timing of Entra Agent ID provisioning depends on the harness that powers the agent.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Agents created before May 2026 continue using traditional app registrations.
claims.quote: Existing agents that you created before Entra Agent ID was implemented in May 2026 continue using traditional app registrations.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: No tenant user, including a tenant administrator, can generate tokens using a Copilot Studio Entra agent identity.
claims.quote: No one in your tenant - including tenant administrators - can generate tokens by using the agent identity.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent's user account is optional.
claims.quote: **Agent's user account (optional)**.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent user account is a different object with a different id from its agent identity.
claims.quote: This second account is a user account in the Microsoft Entra tenant that is decorated as an AI agent. It has a different `id` than the agent identity

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent identity and its user account have a one-to-one relationship.
claims.quote: a 1:1 relationship is always established between an agent identity and its agent's user account.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent user account supports systems that require Microsoft Entra user-account authentication.
claims.quote: Some agents need access to systems that strictly require a Microsoft Entra user account be used for authentication. In these cases, an agent can be given a second account

claims.claim: Dataverse agent users are a preview capability.
claims.quote:
## Create an agent user (preview)

[This section is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The administrator chooses the agent user, adds it to the environment and assigns a security role.
claims.quote: Choose the agent user from the search list, and then select **Add** to add the agent. ... On the **Manage security roles** page, select a security role for your agent.

claims.claim: Federated Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors access data using the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connector write tools initially require explicit user approval.
claims.quote: Tools that create, update, or delete data initially require the user's explicit approval.

claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses subsequent approval prompts for the tool in that conversation.
claims.quote: **Allow for conversation** | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.claim: Always allow can suppress later approval prompts for a federated connector tool.
claims.quote: **Always allow** | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.claim: The federated connector persistent approval choices apply to an individual tool.
claims.quote: **Always allow** and **Allow for conversation** apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector.

claims.claim: Sharing a published agent with triggers for users to run with their own credentials is documented in preview.
claims.quote:
## Share an autonomous agent for users to run (preview)

You can share a published agent that has triggers with users who need to run the agent by using their own credentials.

claims.claim: Sharing an autonomous agent this way requires configuring its triggers and tools for user authentication first.
claims.quote: Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.claim: End-user and maker-provided credential choices are both enabled by default in the administrative control.
claims.quote: By default, both **End-user** and **Maker-provided** credentials are enabled.

claims.claim: The default credential option for connectors and flows is End user credentials.
claims.quote: The default option for connectors and flows is **End user credentials**

claims.claim: Copilot Studio automatically scans and warns makers before publishing when they select maker-provided credentials.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically runs a security scan and warns makers before publishing. ... the security scan provides a warning if the maker changes it to **Maker-provided credentials**.

claims.claim: The cited maker-credential control page names no licence or meter for the setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent identity maker credentials governance authentication. Read configure-no-maker-authentication in full, including its Prerequisites; it names administrative permissions but no licence or meter for this setting.

claims.claim: The cited embedded-credentials setting pages name no licence or meter for that setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials API PowerShell Power Platform. Read configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials in full; neither names a licence or meter for the setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 is one qualifying licence plan for Conditional Access for agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access for agents requires one of the following license plans: ... **Microsoft 365 E7**

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite.
claims.quote: **Microsoft 365 E7**, which includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite.

claims.claim: The alternative licence requirement is Microsoft Agent 365 paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.
claims.quote: **Microsoft Agent 365** license paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.
claims.fix: After the Conditional Access licence bullet, add: "Microsoft's agent-management and disable-agent guides instead state Microsoft Entra ID P1 for configuring these policies; those pages do not repeat the Agent 365 requirement (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/manage-agent-identities-admin and https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/disable-agent-identities)." Keep the dedicated Conditional Access page's stated requirement.

claims.claim: ID Protection for agents requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 during preview.
claims.quote: ID Protection for agents requires a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license during preview.

claims.claim: Every Copilot Studio-created Entra Agent ID counts against the tenant's directory resource quota.
claims.quote: Every Microsoft Entra Agent ID that Copilot Studio creates is a directory object in your tenant and counts against your tenant's resource quota in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: The normal default tenant directory resource quota is 50,000 objects.
claims.quote: **Tenant resource quota**: 50,000 directory objects by default

claims.claim: A verified domain normally raises the tenant resource quota to 300,000 directory objects.
claims.quote: 300,000 if your tenant has a verified domain.

claims.claim: Self-service signup tenants remain at 50,000 objects after domain verification.
claims.quote: Tenants created through self-service signup remain at 50,000 even after a domain is verified.

claims.claim: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totalled and billed through the hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials changes runtime authentication for all tools of all agents in the affected environments immediately.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcing end-user credentials
claims.claim: When maker credentials are prevented, scheduled, autonomous and background agents fail for lack of live user authentication.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials. All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.claim: Entra scope visibility covers Copilot Studio agents regardless of their channel.
claims.quote: Scope **visibility** in Microsoft Entra ID applies to all agents, regardless of channel.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Risks and limits; Open questions
claims.claim: Conditional Access enforcement on Copilot Studio agent-identity connector calls currently applies only in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: Scope **enforcement at runtime** ... currently applies only when the agent runs in **Microsoft Teams** ... Conditional Access on the agent identity isn't yet evaluated for those calls.

claims.claim: Resource access using an API key bypasses Entra token issuance and is not covered by Conditional Access.
claims.quote: if an agent accesses resources using an API key, it bypasses the Microsoft Entra ID authentication and token issuance pipeline entirely and Conditional Access policies won't apply to them.

claims.where: Risks and limits: agent user account
claims.claim: Conditional Access policies targeting agent identities do not apply to their agent user accounts.
claims.quote: A Conditional Access policy targeting agent identities won't apply to the agent's user account.

claims.where: Risks and limits: agent user account
claims.claim: Targeting an agent identity blueprint also does not target the associated agent user accounts.
claims.quote: A Conditional Access policy targeting agent identities using agent identity blueprint covers only the agent identity, not the agent's user account.

claims.where: Risks and limits: agent user account
claims.claim: Agent user accounts need to be separately targeted under Agents in Conditional Access assignments.
claims.quote: to scope policies to agent users, under **Assignments** > **Users, agents, or workload identities**, select **Agents**, and then target all agent users or specific agent users.

claims.where: Risks and limits: embedded-credentials control; Governance controls
claims.claim: The embedded-credentials sharing control governs share and publish time, not runtime blocking.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn't block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: The documented connector-scope behavior applies to first-party and certified Power Platform connectors.
claims.quote: Today, this behavior applies to first-party and certified Power Platform connectors

claims.claim: Custom connectors, MCP servers and REST API tools do not add API permissions to the Entra Agent ID.
claims.quote: custom connectors, MCP servers, and REST API tools added to agents don't add API permissions to the Entra Agent ID.

claims.claim: If the directory quota is reached when the identity is provisioned, the identity and agent fail to be created.
claims.quote: If the tenant reaches its quota at that time, Copilot Studio can't create the Microsoft Entra Agent ID and the agent fails to be created.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Disabling all agent identities
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that globally disabling agent identities can make existing agents fail.
claims.quote: Globally disabling agent identities can cause existing agents to fail

claims.where: Risks and limits: Disabling all agent identities
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that global disabling can push teams toward less transparent application or service principal identities.
claims.quote: push teams to use less transparent application or service principal identities.

claims.claim: Environment Admin can configure the maker-credential control for a single environment.
claims.quote: Environment Admin for a single environment

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator or Global Admin is required to configure maker-credential options for environment groups.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups

claims.claim: Environment-group maker-credential settings override individual environment settings.
claims.quote: environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.claim: Agent ID Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator can manage agent identities.
claims.quote: Manage agent identities | Agent ID Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator

claims.claim: Agent identity owners can manage their own agents without those administrator roles.
claims.quote: Agent identity owners can manage their own agents without these roles.

claims.claim: The update-agentIdentity API page lists AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All as a least-privileged permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All | AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: Configuring Conditional Access policies requires Conditional Access Administrator.
claims.quote: Configure Conditional Access policies | Conditional Access Administrator

claims.claim: Viewing agent sign-in logs requires at least Reports Reader.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a **Reports Reader**.

claims.claim: Agent type and Is Agent filters are available for agent sign-in logs.
claims.quote: **Agent type**: Choose from **Agent ID user**, **Agent Identity**, **Agent Identity Blueprint** or **Not Agentic** ... **Is Agent**: Choose from **No** or **Yes**

claims.claim: A second Microsoft page documents the embedded-credentials control under Security > Threat detection, unlike the environment Features path used in the row.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select **Security**, and then select **Threat detection**. ... Select **Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials**.

claims.claim: No configuration setting is documented for the automatic prepublication security scan.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "security scan" disable configure setting. Read security-scan in full and returned security-and-governance excerpt; both describe automatic warnings, not a configurable scan switch. External threat-detection integration is a separate control.

claims.claim: The maker-credential control pages do not explain interacting-user attribution in connected-service and Copilot audit records.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio maker credentials audit logs interacting user attribution. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials in full; neither specifies audit attribution. Returned general Purview excerpts do not settle connected-service attribution.

claims.claim: Dependency-based enforcement can change which agents the embedded-credentials control treats as unsafe.
claims.quote: As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe dependency can cause the calling agent to be treated as unsafe for sharing.

claims.claim: The embedded-credentials sharing control does not retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn't retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.claim: All sharing allowed detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use without blocking sharing.
claims.quote: All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn't block sharing.

claims.claim: Safe sharing enforced blocks applicable publishing or sharing paths for an unsafe agent.
claims.quote: Safe sharing enforced | Copilot Studio blocks applicable publish or share paths when an agent is unsafe for sharing.

claims.claim: Using a connector with maker-provided credentials requires configuring an authenticated channel.

claims.claim: Administrators can permit maker credentials, end-user credentials or both for tools in an environment or environment group.
